questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: The scatter plot shows hours studied and test scores. Draw a line of fit and write its equation.
questions.prompt_markup:
The scatter plot shows hours studied and test scores.
Draw a line of fit and write its equation.
questions.drawing_answer: A straight line close to the points, with about as many points above it as below it
questions.grading_note: Any equation close to the least-squares line ŷ = 4x + 58.14 (slope about 3.5 to 4.5). The equation should match the student's line.

sections.skill: Evaluate conclusions drawn from a line of fit

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Evaluate conclusions drawn from a line of fit
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: In a study of 7 students, each extra hour of study went with about 4 more points. Can a school claim this holds for all of its students? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
In a study of 7 students, each extra hour of study went with about 4 more points.
Can a school claim this holds for all of its students? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Not with confidence: the sample is small and was not chosen at random, and the study shows association, not cause.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Evaluate conclusions drawn from a line of fit
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A report uses ŷ = 4x + 58 to predict a score of 138 for 20 hours of study. Why is that unreasonable?
questions.prompt_markup:
A report uses ŷ = 4x + 58 to predict a score of 138 for 20 hours of study.
Why is that unreasonable?
questions.correct_answer: 20 hours is far outside the data (1 to 7 hours), and scores cannot exceed 100.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation.

questions.correct_answer: The data came from a large random sample.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Use simulation to judge whether an association could be due to chance
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: The test scores were randomly re-paired with the study hours 1,000 times, and the slope was never as large as 4. What does that suggest?
questions.prompt_markup:
The test scores were randomly re-paired with the study hours 1,000 times, and the slope was never as large as 4.
What does that suggest?
questions.correct_answer: The association is very unlikely to be due to chance alone.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions

questions.prompt: In an experiment, a tutoring group averaged 6 points more than a control group. Random regroupings gave differences of 6 or more 30% of the time. What is the conclusion?
questions.prompt_markup:
In an experiment, a tutoring group averaged 6 points more than a control group. Random regroupings gave differences of 6 or more 30% of the time.
What is the conclusion?
questions.correct_answer: The difference is not significant; it could easily be due to chance.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the conclusion with the reason.
